page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.large is an x86_64 virtual server from the high-clock-speed family, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB core running at a 3.3 GHz base frequency. The hardware includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory capacity is fixed at 16.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached volumes and offering a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a split profile dictated by core counts and clock speeds. Single-core performance sits in the middle tiers, evidenced by a stress-ng score of 1573.79, a Geekbench single-core score of 1327.0, and 26.65 GB/s gzip compression throughput. In contrast, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, resulting in lower scores across multi-threaded stress-ng (2071.39) and Geekbench (1591.0). Uncached memory bandwidth tests record 15.43 GB/s for reads and 13.17 GB/s for writes, accompanied by Redis performance of 2.01 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, ecs.hfr7.large delivers high per-core memory capacity and dedicated frequency without the overhead of larger socket allocations. The primary engineering tradeoff is the strict reliance on remote block storage and bounded multi-threaded processing power. Consequently, this instance serves best for small memory-focused workloads, in-memory caching tiers, lightweight relational databases, and background processing tasks that benefit from clock speed and memory headroom over raw core density.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.large is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by a dedicated 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs from a single physical hyper-threaded core, supported by 16 GB of memory to achieve an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The system includes 33 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 extensions, and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while omitting local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid single-core execution alongside restricted multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics resulting from the compact core configuration. Cost efficiency is defined by dedicated clock cycles and generous per-vCPU memory density without requiring larger core footprints. The ecs.hfr7.large is suitable for lightweight in-memory caching, single-threaded batch processing, network-storage backed databases, and utility services requiring memory headroom.
